samplePassage: We give checkout a separate pool of workers so a slow inventory lookup cannot consume every available connection.

cases.question: How would you keep a slow dependency from taking down the checkout service?
cases.answer: I would start by isolating inventory. We give checkout a separate pool of workers so a slow inventory lookup cannot consume every available connection. Then I would measure how long customers wait during recovery.

sources.label: Practice answer
sources.text: Start by limiting the blast radius. We give checkout a separate pool of workers so a slow inventory lookup cannot consume every available connection. A timeout places a bound on the wait.

cases.question: How would you verify that the enclosure is safe to open?
cases.answer: Technicians isolate the battery before opening the enclosure and test both terminals with an independent meter. I would document the reading and the isolation point.

sources.label: Practice answer
sources.text: Technicians isolate the battery before opening the enclosure and test both terminals with an independent meter. Keep a written record.

sources.label: Permitted service manual
sources.text: Technicians isolate the battery before opening the enclosure and test both terminals with an independent meter.

cases.question: Which measurement changed your rollout plan?
cases.answer: At our staging site I compared the oldest pending message before and after restarting the slow consumer. The queue recovered faster when we limited concurrent retries.
